Legacy contract review text for 'polar-api-credential' (verbatim legacy text; the date is the dossier researchedAt, not the authoring date): Arrival evidence (#528, product redact-secret#1020; #1014 handoff polar.md, READY). Personal access tokens, OAuth access and refresh tokens, the OAuth client secret and the client registration token act for a user or an organization, or let an integration mint tokens. T1 under R1 and R9: the prefix constants and both eras are the provider's server code. The grammar is the union of the two issued grammars: an era-1 body is 43 URL-safe bytes, an era-2 body is 43 alphanumerics (a subset), and no checksum applies to these roles because an era-1 body is all-alphanumeric about a quarter of the time. polar_pat_ is no longer minted but existing tokens are accepted. polar_at_ without its u_/o_ sub-type is not a prefix. The body class contains _ and -, so a trailing byte lengthens the run and no trailing-glue twin is authored (#84). Neither pinned peer has a Polar rule.

Evidence-class review for #64, read 2026-10-03 (research-agent, automation; not reviewed). 11 negative fixtures held as project-policy. Re-based to provider-documented on Polar server source at 6a4f2f6: unknown-role-twin (the prefix constants yield no polar_rx_; no occurrence in the tree at that commit) and uppercase-prefix-twin (prefix is the lower-case literal). Kept project-policy: access-token-without-subtype-twin (an earlier revision, 9b228a96d7 of 2024-03-29, defined polar_at_ and polar_rt_ with no sub-type letter; changed in 27a004c4e0 on 2024-04-24; whether it was ever issued is not established); body-42, body-44, dot-in-body, setting-names, truncated-near-miss (an era-1 body is prefix + secrets.token_urlsafe(); its 43-character length and alphabet come from the Python standard library default, not a Polar statement, and era-1 tokens may still be accepted; only the era-2 generator states 43 of [A-Za-z0-9]); body-44 and leading-glue also rest on a token boundary that no source states (contract claim field-boundary is unresolved); checkout-link-secret-public-id (the polar_cl_ value is the secret in checkout link URLs that the docs tell sellers to share; deriving non-confidentiality takes two statements, so it is inferred) and client-id-in-url-public-id (Polar OAuth client setup page says the Client ID and Client Secret values are super sensitive and should be kept secret, while Polar open-source clients embed their own polar_ci_ ids; unsettled). Peer artifacts: only betterleaks has a Polar rule (regex polar_(oat|pat|at)_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,100}), plus ports of it; no second maintainer found (CredSweeper, detect-secrets, trivy, titus not searched: rate limit); that regex accepts 42 and 44 character bodies. Not a support-status decision.
